title: 写策略：写直达 vs 写回的主存写次数
expected_output:
=== write-through vs write-back ===
  208 write operations total (first 8 hit the SAME block)

  policy                             main-memory writes
  write-through + no-write-allocate           208
  write-back + write-allocate                 137

reading the numbers:
  a write-through cache pays one memory write per store: 208
  a write-back cache pays one memory write per EVICTED DIRTY line: 137
  the 8 repeated writes to one block cost 8 vs 1 in memory traffic

trade-offs:
  write-through : simple, memory always up to date, but high bandwidth cost
  write-back    : low bandwidth, but needs a dirty bit and is harder to keep coherent
  real CPUs use write-back + write-allocate; caches are then made coherent by
  protocols such as MESI, whose state transitions are what false sharing disturbs.
code:
BLOCK = 16

# 一段"写密集"的工作负载：固定模式，保证输出可复现
# 前 8 次反复写同一个块（模拟循环里反复更新同一变量）
# 之后顺序写 200 个不同的块（模拟大范围写入）
WRITES = [0x0000] * 8 + [b * BLOCK for b in range(1, 201)]

def write_through():
    """写直达 + 写不分配：每次写都打到主存"""
    return len(WRITES)

def write_back():
    """写回 + 写分配：脏块只在被替换时写回一次"""
    dirty = set()          # 当前被写脏（尚未写回）的块
    flushed = 0
    cache_lines = 64       # 1 KB / 16 B，直接映射
    resident = {}
    for a in WRITES:
        blk = a // BLOCK
        idx = blk % cache_lines
        if resident.get(idx) != blk:
            # 发生替换：若被换出的是脏块，则需写回主存
            if idx in dirty:
                flushed += 1
                dirty.discard(idx)
            resident[idx] = blk
        dirty.add(idx)
    return flushed

print("=== write-through vs write-back ===")
print("  %d write operations total (first 8 hit the SAME block)" % len(WRITES))
print()
print("  %-34s %12s" % ("policy", "main-memory writes"))
print("  %-34s %12d" % ("write-through + no-write-allocate", write_through()))
print("  %-34s %12d" % ("write-back + write-allocate", write_back()))
print()
print("reading the numbers:")
print("  a write-through cache pays one memory write per store: %d" % write_through())
print("  a write-back cache pays one memory write per EVICTED DIRTY line: %d" % write_back())
print("  the 8 repeated writes to one block cost 8 vs 1 in memory traffic")
print()
print("trade-offs:")
print("  write-through : simple, memory always up to date, but high bandwidth cost")
print("  write-back    : low bandwidth, but needs a dirty bit and is harder to keep coherent")
print("  real CPUs use write-back + write-allocate; caches are then made coherent by")
print("  protocols such as MESI, whose state transitions are what false sharing disturbs.")
